blocks.content: The Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the House of the People.

rows: Wider body consisting of 60 to 70 ministers
Smaller body consisting of 15 to 20 senior ministers
Includes Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers
Includes only Cabinet Ministers holding key portfolios
Does not meet as a single body to transact official government business
Meets regularly as a body to deliberate, formulate policy, and take executive decisions
Vested with full constitutional status under original Articles 74 and 75
Inserted into Article 352 in 1978 by the 44th Amendment Act

items: Collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha alone, not to the Rajya Sabha or Parliament as a whole.
The word 'Cabinet' was not present in the original Constitution; it was inserted into Article 352 by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.
Under Article 74(2), the advice tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in any court of law.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 74 mandates a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President in exercising constitutional functions.
By the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, the total number of ministers including the PM cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible strictly to the Lok Sabha (House of the People) under Article 75(3).
Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, which embodies the principle of individual responsibility.
The Council of Ministers includes Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers, whereas the Cabinet includes only Cabinet Ministers.
